text: Flash cards of flash memory? Nope, here's the real scoop! Every SSD is a little superhero powered by NAND flash cells, and TLC (triple-level cell) flash, the everyday workhorse in most drives, is good for roughly 3,000 write cycles per cell before it starts to fade. Sounds limited, right? Not with the clever tricks inside your drive! Wear leveling is the star of the show: it spreads your writes evenly across every block, so no single cell gets overworked while its neighbors sit idle. Think of it as a fair-share team plan where everybody pitches in! Then there's over-provisioning, typically around 7%, a hidden reserve of spare flash that the controller uses to swap out worn blocks and keep performance humming. Together, these features stretch those 3,000 cycles across years of everyday use, so your drive can keep handling your photos, games, and work files with confidence. Pretty amazing engineering, honestly!
